title: Why Is Printer Ink So Expensive?
description:
Printers are often sold at a loss because the real money is in the ink, and HP's printing business earns nearly four times the margin of its PCs.
#printerink #hp #money #shorts

Sources: Consumer Reports (printer ink and wasted ink investigations); U.S. PIRG; The Register (Jan 19, 2024); PetaPixel (Jan 24, 2024); TechRadar (Jan 22, 2024); HotHardware (2024); Techlicious (Jan 1, 2025); HP Q3 fiscal 2026 results (Aug 2026); Print in the Channel (Aug 28, 2026)
Photos: cartridgesaveimages, freestockimages, spacekermit, Rellenadodecartuchos, leokoivulehto (CC BY, Flickr)
tags: why is printer ink so expensive
first_comment: Be honest: do you buy HP brand ink, or the cheap third-party cartridges? 🖨️

scenes.say: Your printer was sold at a loss on purpose.
scenes.source: Consumer Reports citing IHS Markit (cost to build a printer is higher than the retail price of most consumer printers; classic razor-and-blade model); U.S. PIRG (makers sell printers at a loss to lock buyers into ink); TechRadar Jan 22 2024 (HP CEO confirmed a loss on many models)

scenes.say: HP's CEO calls every printer it sells an investment.
scenes.source: The Register Jan 19 2024 (Lores on CNBC: 'Every time a customer buys a printer, it's an investment for us'); PetaPixel Jan 24 2024 (same remark)

scenes.say: So how do they make money?
The ink. HP cartridges can cost over {$40|forty dollars} an ounce.
scenes.source: Techlicious Jan 1 2025 (HP 962 standard cartridge $40.22 per ounce); Consumer Reports wasted-ink investigation (HP 64XL about $93 per ounce)

scenes.say: And Consumer Reports found many printers put half or less of your ink on the page.

visual.caption: or less of your ink reaches the page

scenes.source: Consumer Reports wasted-ink investigation ('many models delivered half or less of their ink to the page'); U.S. PIRG citing Consumer Reports (more than half of the ink you buy never winds up on a page, with many printers)

scenes.say: But here's the interesting part. Use a cartridge HP says violates its {IP|I P}, and its CEO says they stop the printer.
scenes.source: The Register Jan 19 2024 (Lores: 'when we identify cartridges that are violating our IP, we stop the printers from work[ing]'); HotHardware 2024 (same quote)

scenes.say: And customers who skip HP's ink? He told CNBC, it's a bad investment.
scenes.source: The Register Jan 19 2024 and PetaPixel Jan 24 2024 (Lores: if a customer 'doesn't print enough or doesn't use our supplies, it's a bad investment'); HotHardware 2024

scenes.say: HP's printing business earns an {18%|eighteen percent} margin. Its PC business? Under {5%|five}.
scenes.source: HP Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings release, 8-K Aug 2026 (Printing 18.1% operating margin, Personal Systems 4.6%); Print in the Channel Aug 28 2026 (same figures)

scenes.say: So the printer was never the product. The ink is. That's why
scenes.source: Loop line into the hook; summary, no new figure
